description: FRED claim registry. Schema: docs/architecture.md (repository). Status and review_state semantics: references/evidence-policy.md.

claims.claim: Official firmware release 1.5.1 corresponds to commit 9e810dc399e027e48ce07751df72168abbb19065.
claims.consequence: Record the exact commit, never 'latest'.

claims.claim: targets/f7/api_symbols.csv at the baseline declares API version 88.2 and lists exported (+) and unexported (-) symbols with full signatures.
claims.consequence: Export membership and signatures are compatibility inputs; re-read this row at every baseline review.

claims.claim: The official update index publishes the f7 SDK for 1.5.1 at https://update.flipperzero.one/builds/firmware/1.5.1/flipper-z-f7-sdk-1.5.1.zip with SHA-256 dfde39df32ba8a9789b26afc1d702579ad8399a1c285770637cfe3287b2e2ffe; a download on 2026-10-16 matched this digest and its api_symbols.csv is byte-identical to the pinned firmware table.

sources.locator: release channel, version 1.5.1, target f7, type sdk_zip

claims.consequence: Use this URL and digest for the baseline SDK; verify bytes again on every new setup.

claims.claim: uFBT 0.2.6 builds from the app directory into dist, downloads SDK and toolchain on first run from the release channel by default, selects SDKs with update --branch/--url/--local, and stores state in UFBT_HOME (default ~/.ufbt); 'ufbt update --local' additionally requires --hw-target.
claims.consequence: Pin SDK and bootstrap separately and isolate UFBT_HOME; first run is a download with external effects.

claims.claim: Official dev at 3fb1d51 declares API 88.4 and exports 42 symbols absent from 1.5.1, with no removed exports or signature changes (compare_api.py over both pinned tables).
claims.consequence: A FAP built against dev can import symbols missing on 1.5.1; dev is not the baseline.

claims.claim: Flipper Zero uses a monochrome 128x64 LCD and an STM32WB55 with 256 KB SRAM shared between firmware, radio stack and applications.
claims.consequence: No fixed application heap allowance; design for LCD constraints.

claims.claim: malloc is exported (Function,+,malloc) and implemented as pvPortMalloc on the firmware heap.
claims.consequence: Do not flag malloc as forbidden.

claims.claim: pvPortMalloc crashes with 'memmgt in ISR' in IRQ mode and fails furi_check with 'out of memory' or 'malloc(0)' instead of returning NULL.

sources.locator: pvPortMalloc(): FURI_IS_IRQ_MODE check and final furi_check

claims.consequence: Bound sizes before allocating; NULL checks do not make OOM recoverable; never allocate in IRQ.

claims.claim: api_symbols.csv at the baseline has no furi_alloc row; no universal furi_alloc requirement is established.
claims.consequence: Do not invent or require furi_alloc. Absence of a row does not by itself prove absence of a macro.

claims.claim: FAP code, data and constant sections are loaded into RAM by the ELF loader and their imports are resolved against the firmware API table.
claims.consequence: Budget code, constants and assets as RAM; missing imports fail at load time.

claims.claim: Generic App() requires appid and apptype; application.fam is Python syntax evaluated by the build; catalog submission adds separate requirements.
claims.consequence: Read manifests and hooks before building; helpers must never eval manifests.

claims.claim: A public FAP capability requires a header, an implementation, an exported row or declared library, a resource owner and a successful build; a header alone does not establish availability.
claims.consequence: Trace header to export to build before advising an API.

claims.claim: The baseline exports __wrap_printf, __wrap_snprintf and __wrap_vsnprintf while the raw printf row is not exported; the print library wraps calls at link time.
claims.consequence: Raw symbol status alone is misleading; prefer FURI_LOG and bounded snprintf; verify output route.

claims.claim: furi_record_open increments a holder count and waits until the record exists; furi_record_close decrements it; destroy is refused while holders remain.
claims.consequence: Balance borrows, never free services, verify names; a misspelled name blocks forever; a missing close is an imbalance, not a guaranteed panic.

claims.claim: No RECORD_PASSTHROUGH definition was established in the inspected public surface.
claims.consequence: Treat as invented until a defining header is found at the pin.

claims.claim: furi_message_queue_put/get in IRQ or masked context require a non-NULL message and zero timeout, otherwise furi_check fails.
claims.consequence: IRQ producers use zero-timeout operations and an explicit full-queue policy.

claims.claim: furi_timer_stop calls xTimerStop and returns; it does not wait for an in-flight callback, although timer.h describes it as synchronous until the timer queue is processed.
claims.consequence: Stopping is not a callback barrier; keep callback context alive until furi_timer_free returns.

claims.claim: furi_timer_free deletes the timer and then calls furi_timer_flush, which pends a function on the timer daemon and waits for it.
claims.consequence: Calling free/flush from a timer callback would wait on the daemon from the daemon (inferred deadlock); free from app thread.

claims.claim: furi_timer_alloc, start, stop and free furi_check that they are not called from IRQ or masked context.
claims.consequence: Signal from IRQ to a thread; manage timers from threads.

claims.claim: ViewPort draw and input callbacks are documented as called from the GUI thread; ViewDispatcher event callbacks run in the thread running the dispatcher.
claims.consequence: Keep GUI callbacks short; handle events in the app thread.

claims.claim: view_port_alloc, view_dispatcher_alloc and scene_manager_alloc are all exported; SceneManager is optional.
claims.consequence: Choose the smallest UI architecture.

claims.claim: Storage API calls post a message to the storage service and wait for completion (S_API_EPILOGUE); read/write return byte counts.
claims.consequence: Storage blocks the caller; keep it out of GUI/timer/IRQ callbacks and check counts.

claims.claim: Power-loss atomicity of storage rename/sync on the SD filesystem is not established.
claims.consequence: Use temp file plus recovery; never promise atomic settings writes.

claims.claim: Native file formats are distinct schemas; Infrared .ir uses 'Filetype: IR signals file', 'Version: 1', parsed (protocol, 4-byte address/command) and raw (frequency, duty_cycle, up to 1024 timings) signals.
claims.consequence: Validate body fields, not just the header; bounded subset parsers state their subset.

claims.claim: gap_init configures the BLE GAP with GAP_PERIPHERAL_ROLE at the baseline.
claims.consequence: The stock FAP surface is a BLE peripheral.

claims.claim: No general BLE central/GATT-client workflow is exported: no aci_gap_create_connection, aci_gatt_disc_*, aci_gatt_read_char_* or aci_gatt_write_char_* rows; exported ble_gatt_* functions are server-side.

sources.locator: absence of central/client rows; ble_gatt_* rows

claims.consequence: Appliance controllers needing central role go to a host or verified companion MCU.

claims.claim: furi_hal_serial_control_acquire returns NULL if the interface is in use; serial async and DMA RX callbacks run in interrupt context.
claims.consequence: Check acquisition; keep RX callbacks IRQ-safe and bounded.

claims.claim: I2C, SPI, ADC and PWM have exported acquire/use/release or start/stop APIs (for example furi_hal_i2c_acquire, furi_hal_spi_acquire, furi_hal_adc_acquire, furi_hal_pwm_start).
claims.consequence: Use acquire/release with timeouts; pins, units and DMA contracts need per-path inspection.

claims.claim: Header I/O pins (2-7, 10, 12-17) are 3.3 V CMOS logic, connected to STM32WB55RG pins through 51 Ohm series resistors with ESD protection; each can source up to 20 mA (absolute maximum per pin; sum over all I/O 100 mA) and +5V/+3.3V header supplies allow 1.2 A each. All 13 are FT-family pins, but 5 V input is allowed only with the MCU powered, internal pulls disabled and no analog function; firmware 1.5.1 sets every non-debug header pin to analog mode at early init. The two official pages conflict ('+3.3 V tolerant' vs 'Input 5 V tolerant').

sources.locator: I/O pins; 51 Ohm resistors; 20 mA per pin; 5 W total; 3.3 V and 5 V tolerance
GPIO row: Input 5 V tolerant (See AN4899)
STM32WB55 DS11929 Rev 18: Table 16 pin structures, Tables 20-21 absolute maximum ratings, Table 24 note 4-5
gpio_pins[] header mapping; furi_hal_resources_init_early sets header pins to GpioModeAnalog

claims.consequence: Treat every header pin as 3.3 V only; never connect 5 V signals directly; budget at most 20 mA per pin (about 8 mA at rated logic levels) and 100 mA total. Use level shifting for 5 V modules.
claims.notes: Unresolved: the primary AN4899 text on analog-mode tolerance (only an ST community quote was available), the schematic PDFs (official links expired) and the ESD part ratings.

claims.claim: Flipper Zero operates as a USB device with selectable interfaces (CDC, HID); it is not a general USB host.
claims.consequence: Do not design for USB host peripherals; restore replaced configuration.

claims.claim: Flipper JavaScript runs on a vendored, modified mJS core with firmware modules (JS SDK 1.0). A host build of the pinned core shows: no closures over outer locals, no try/catch/throw, no JSON, no arrow functions, classes, template literals, async or Promise, no Array map/forEach/join, == rejected and implicit number/string conversion prohibited; let/const work. It is not Node or browser JavaScript.

sources.locator: mjs_parser.c parse_statement; mjs_builtin.c (JSON commented out); mjs_exec.c

claims.consequence: JS guidance is feasibility-only; never assume closures, exceptions, JSON or array higher-order functions; module behavior on device is untested.
claims.notes: Host evidence: docs/research/evidence/2026-10-16-mjs (core interpreter only, not device behavior).

claims.claim: Official firmware unit tests run on-device using a dedicated firmware app set.
claims.consequence: Host tests complement but do not replace device tests.

claims.claim: SWD/GDB FAP debugging requires a supported probe and firmware, ELF and SDK that match.
claims.consequence: Collect matching identities before debugging.

claims.claim: The ZDStudios fapemu runner executes FAP Thumb code on a Unicorn Cortex-M4 model with about 152 Python handlers for API 87.1; any other import silently returns 0, 19 handlers are no-ops, there is no scheduler, peripheral, radio, ViewDispatcher or API-version check, and the repository's LICENSE is empty. No comprehensive official emulator exists.
claims.consequence: Emulator runs are at most smoke evidence for relocation and simple ViewPort logic, never hardware or compatibility evidence; 'ran without fault' is weak because missing APIs succeed silently. Nothing may be copied.

claims.claim: ufbt lint runs lint.py check and ufbt format runs lint.py format (clang-format and naming); there is no ufbt test target.
claims.consequence: Report lint as formatting evidence; never invent ufbt test.

claims.claim: In a prepared firmware tree, ./fbt build APPSRC=applications_user/<path> builds without uploading, ./fbt fap_<appid> builds an external app, and FIRMWARE_APP_SET=unit_tests updater_package builds the on-device test firmware.
claims.consequence: Firmware builds can fetch toolchains on first run; unit_tests package is not a host test.

claims.claim: The pinned catalog bundler runs ufbt update, clones source and submodules, and normally lints and builds; requirements include dataclass-wizard, Pillow, PyYAML, Markdown, uFBT and requests.
claims.consequence: Bundling has download/build effects and needs scoped authority.

claims.claim: Catalog AGENTS.md asks for 512x256 qFlipper-palette screenshots while the bundler accepts 4x or 8x scale factors.
claims.consequence: Follow the stricter documented workflow; validator acceptance is not policy compliance.

claims.claim: Momentum, Unleashed and Xtreme are separate lineages with different API tables. At the pinned heads: Momentum d3f89df declares API 87.1 (468 exports added, 2 removed, 1 signature changed vs official 88.2); Unleashed f62964c declares '88.20' and is a superset (312 added, 0 removed, 0 changed); archived Xtreme 54619d0 declares 58.1 (443 added, 336 removed, 120 changed) and uses toolchain 33. JS modules also differ: Momentum and Unleashed add blebeacon, i2c, spi, infrared, subghz, usbdisk and vgm.
claims.consequence: No fork support claimed. A Momentum or Xtreme build is rejected by the official loader (API major differs); an Unleashed build passes the manifest check but fails if it imports any Unleashed-only symbol. Rebuild against the official SDK.

claims.claim: Building the pinned firmware tree with a non-official toolchain (Ubuntu arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.1, newlib 4.4) made the SDK API generator drop ten __retarget_lock_* exports and fbt rewrote targets/f7/api_symbols.csv to version 89.0.
claims.consequence: Pin the official toolchain as well as uFBT and the SDK; a different compiler/newlib can silently change the declared API.
claims.notes: Observed by executing fbt on 2026-10-16; record in evaluations/results/2026-10-16-sdk-qualification.

claims.claim: The 1.5.1 SDK uses Flipper toolchain version 39 (arm-none-eabi-gcc 12.3.1 20230626, GNU ld 2.40), downloaded by uFBT from update.flipperzero.one without a published checksum file.
claims.consequence: Record toolchain version and compiler identity in every build report; the archive hash can only be observed, not publisher-verified.

claims.claim: fbt's GatherSources() deduplicates an app's sources patterns with list(set(...)) before globbing them, and the external-app build compiles and links the result in that order; with more than one pattern, object order follows the Python hash seed of the SCons process, which uFBT 0.2.6 neither sets nor clears.
claims.consequence: Multi-source FAP hashes vary between clean builds unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed; sorting the sources list has no effect.
claims.notes: Replayed with Python 3.13 and matched to the 2026-10-16 SDK qualification hashes; confirmed with SDK 1.5.1 and toolchain 39: seed 0 gave one hash over five clean builds, seed 1 reversed the compile order. Record in evaluations/results/2026-10-16-build-reproducibility.

claims.claim: fbt makes the .fap from the debug ELF with objcopy --strip-debug --strip-unneeded --add-gnu-debuglink, so the .fap keeps a .gnu_debuglink section holding the debug ELF's name and a CRC-32 of that whole file, whose DWARF records absolute source and SDK paths.
claims.consequence: The same app built from a different folder or UFBT_HOME gives a different .fap hash; compare hashes only between builds with identical absolute paths.
claims.notes: Mechanism reproduced with host gcc 13.3/binutils 2.42 and confirmed with toolchain 39: across two app folders only .gnu_debuglink differed for all six FRED fixtures. Record in evaluations/results/2026-10-16-build-reproducibility.

claims.claim: The official 1.5.1 loader rejects a FAP only for a hardware-target mismatch or a different API major (ApiTooOld/ApiTooNew); the API-minor comparisons are commented out, so minor differences surface only as unresolved imports during ELF symbol resolution.
claims.consequence: A matching major does not mean an app loads: check every import against the target's api_symbols.csv. A newer-minor app loads only if it uses no newer symbols.

claims.claim: VariableItemList value counts and current indices are uint8_t, and a View's previous_callback is invoked from ViewDispatcher's Back-input handling (view_dispatcher.c) through view_previous (view.c).
claims.consequence: Map wide setting ranges onto at most 255 steps; keep previous callbacks free of storage or slow work.
